title: Elastic working-set profiles and on-the-fly micro-quantization for graceful OOM avoidance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We continue to see tail OOMs in mixed-workload nodes where large-context chats and high-throughput short requests share the same GPU pools. Existing mitigation (strict admission + coarse eviction) causes high latency spikes or rejects requests aggressively. This ticket proposes a two-part runtime feature: (1) per-model working-set profiles that predict typical KV footprint and hot-region density, and (2) an on-the-fly micro-quantization path that can transparently reduce per-request KV residency for low-risk batches to avoid OOM while preserving fidelity for high-priority traffic. The goal is graceful degradation rather than hard failures: attempt lightweight memory reduction first, then progressively apply cheaper fallbacks before rejecting or switching model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Working-set profiling service running in runtime - collects per-model KPIs (avg KV bytes per active stream, hot-key skew, median sequence-length distribution) and exposes a compressed profile API.
Micro-quantization path implemented in inference runtime - can switch to a 4-bit proxy for cached KV shards at batch admission time with <6% median quality delta on benchmark prompts.
Admission controller integrates profiles and micro-quant path - admission logic reduces KV allocation for opportunistic batches when predicted headroom < configured threshold.
End-to-end integration test that injects synthetic memory pressure and demonstrates 80% fewer hard OOMs compared to baseline admission+eviction policy in the lab harness.
Metrics and dashboard: per-node OOM count, micro-quant usage rate, request-level fidelity delta histogram, and customer_error_rate displayed on Console runtime-1.22 dashboard.
Feature flagging and canary rollout docs exist - default off for Dedicated clusters; opt-in flag for Private deployments.
tasks: Instrument runtime to emit per-request KV residency samples and aggregate per-model histograms (ENG changes)
Design a compact on-disk working-set profile format and a lightweight in-memory cache for fast lookups (ENG + runtime infra)
Implement micro-quantization conversion for cached KV shards with zero-copy path where possible (inference-engine)
Extend admission controller to consult profiles + headroom heuristic and toggle micro-quant path (or signal fallback to lower-fidelity model)
Create an integration test harness that reproduces mixed large/short workload OOMs and verifies recovery steps
Add Console metrics + alerting rules and a small UX card explaining micro-quant events to operators
decisions: We will prefer opportunistic micro-quantization to full model swapping because it preserves latency and avoids cold-starts for many bursts.
Quantization granularity: implement per-KV-shard micro-quant first (fewer code changes) and evaluate per-layer in follow-up if needed.
Profile TTL: working-set profiles will be considered stale after 24 hours; runtime will fall back to a conservative default when profiles are missing.
Safety knob: a request with "never-degrade" header (internal priority) will never be subject to micro-quantization and instead triggers model fallback or admission reject.
Privacy: profiles contain only aggregate numeric footprints and sketch IDs, no user data; security review deemed low risk (see security_notes).
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.elastic_working_set = false by default
Phase 1 (lab): enable on canary nodes running synthetic mixed workload to validate OOM reduction (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (staging): roll to 5% of hosted clusters with telemetry collection and auto-rollback on fidelity regressions (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual): staged rollout to Dedicated customers as opt-in, Private customers can enable via config; monitor Console metrics and customer tickets for 4 weeks
Rollback: immediate disable of micro-quant path and revert to baseline admission if OOM rate rises or fidelity regressions exceed threshold
metrics: Target: reduce hard OOM rate by >= 70% for mixed-workload nodes in lab harness
Quality: median log-prob delta <= 0.06 across standard eval prompts when micro-quant is used
Performance: micro-quant path adds <= 3ms median admission overhead
Adoption: micro-quant used for <= 30% of short/high-throughput batches initially (configurable)
